repository.title: Datacenter Infrastructure Lab
repository.description: Explore data center power continuity, energy ledgers & infrastructure assumptions through reproducible synthetic models.
repository.summary: The native lab models outages, source paths, finite reserve, and exact energy accounting alongside infrastructure lessons. This companion isolates an illustrative IT-load and cooling-power relationship.
repository.audience: Datacenter engineers, infrastructure students, and researchers examining electrical continuity assumptions.

model.equation: u = clamp(U + 8 sin(t/8) + 3 cos(t/3), 0, 100); IT = N(0.12 + 0.38u/100); cooling = IT/COP · (1 + 0.025 max(Tₐ−20, 0)); PUE = 1 + cooling/IT.
assumptions: Synthetic repeatable workload waves replace production utilization telemetry.
Each server draws 0.12–0.50 kW; cooling COP is a constant simplified efficiency.
Inlet temperature relaxes toward a heuristic operating point; airflow, humidity, and equipment limits are omitted.
Server counts and workload oscillations are invented; no GPU throughput, real facility telemetry, or equipment availability is inferred.
The displayed facility/IT ratio includes only the modeled cooling overhead, not all facility loads or annual measured PUE.
This companion does not simulate UPS depletion, chiller outage cascades, protection coordination, server reboots, or certified uptime.
model.introduction: A synthetic server workload drives a simplified cooling-power screen. The native outage experiment, its 100 kWh reference case, and its source-path/energy ledger remain separate reproducible entry points.

modules.title: Build an electrical load ledger
modules.objective: Distinguish IT power from facility overhead and from stored energy.
steps: Read the canonical outage case and identify which quantities are kW and which are kWh.
Apply 100 synthetic servers, 65% utilization, 20°C outside temperature, and COP 4.
Run to thirty minutes and compare IT power, cooling power, and their ratio.
modules.reflection: Why cannot this instantaneous cooling ratio be described as the facility’s measured annual PUE?

modules.title: Scale the population while holding efficiency
modules.objective: Identify which outputs scale with server count and which are ratios.
steps: Double server count to 200 and retain the baseline utilization, ambient, and COP.
Predict the changes in IT and cooling power before running.
Relate the larger demand to the finite-reserve question in the native continuity model.

checkpoints.label: Scaled IT power at thirty minutes

modules.reflection: If usable stored energy stays fixed, what would a higher electrical demand imply for ride-through duration, and which native model can calculate it?

modules.title: Stress an ambient and efficiency assumption
modules.objective: Quantify a cooling-power sensitivity without inventing a reliability result.
steps: Use 200 servers at 65% utilization, raise outside temperature to 40°C, and set COP to 3.
Predict the change in cooling overhead and run to thirty minutes.
Identify the chiller, airflow, humidity, redundancy, and equipment-limit evidence absent from this screen.
modules.reflection: Why does a warmer modeled inlet temperature not establish a server failure or a containment-breach time?

modules.title: Connect the screen to continuity evidence
modules.objective: Prepare a bounded infrastructure comparison and choose the native follow-up study.
steps: Retain the hot 200-server case and improve assumed COP from 3 to 5.
Run and export the comparison with its inputs and synthetic-data label.
Open the canonical outage source and explain its distinction between ride-through duration and elapsed depletion timestamp.
modules.reflection: What additional scenario inputs and independent evidence would be needed to turn a cooling-power sensitivity into a facility continuity study?
